title: Safety Dial: Operations Play (scratch)
body:
TL;DR
Have a lightweight, adjustable "safety dial" to control risk during model flips and incremental rollouts. Use staged cohorts + automatic rollback triggers + a small warmup phase to reduce token error spikes. This is a working checklist and runbook sketch — notes to self.

Goals
- Keep user-facing error rate degradation < 0.5% absolute during ramp.
- Keep median inference latency within +20% of baseline for first 10k requests.
- Detect quality regressions early via small prompt set and user-keyed checks.

Success criteria (for green release)
- 48h window: no more than 3 incidents requiring manual rollback.
- Baseline metrics (latency P50/P95, error rate) within thresholds defined below.
- No sustained increase in user-reported problem tickets vs previous week.

Preflight checklist (quick run before flip)
- [ ] Verify model artifact checksum and container image tag (sha): note tag and attestation.
- [ ] Smoke run on staging: run 500 requests with production-like sequences, compare tokens/latency.
- [ ] Canary infra primed (reserved warm GPUs up, KV cache priming script ready).
- [ ] Alerting hooks created for the experiment (PagerDuty escalation path confirmed).
- [ ] Add rollout metadata to analytics and logging (version tag, cohort id).
- [ ] Confirm fallback target (previous model tag) is available in all target regions.

Cohort design and ramp schedule (Safety Dial positions)
- Dial 0 — hold: no traffic.
- Dial 1 — anchor (0.05% traffic, ~first 200 qps across all customers, default low-risk tenants). Hold 30m.
- Dial 2 — small (1% traffic, selected low-impact tenants + internal users). Hold 2h.
- Dial 3 — steady (5% traffic, broader but still non-critical customers). Hold 4h.
- Dial 4 — wide (25% traffic). Hold 12h and evaluate.
- Dial 5 — full (100% traffic). Post-rollout monitoring for 72h.

Notes on cohort selection
- Prefer customers with low SLAs and/or internal sandbox tenants for early steps.
- Use SDK feature flag + routing rules to pin cohorts. Avoid cookie-based routing for first two steps.

Telemetry (minimum set to monitor)
- request_success_rate (per-version, per-region)
- per_token_error_rate (internal parse/extract failures)
- latency_p50/p95/p99 (per-version)
- tokens_per_request distribution (to detect early token blow-ups)
- backend_gpu_util and queue_length (resource pressure)
- E2E user funnel errors (client-side logs aggregated)
- promptset regression score (run curated 120 prompts every 30m)

Thresholds and automatic actions
- If request_success_rate drops >1.5 percentage points vs baseline for 15m -> automatically pin back to previous model and notify on #releases.
- If latency_p95 increases by >100% vs baseline for 10m and GPU queue > 100 -> scale up burst pool and pause ramp.
- If promptset regression score drops > 5% (absolute) -> immediate rollback to previous tag (auto).
- If tokens_per_request median increases > 2x for >30m -> pause rollout and investigate prompt changes.

Pinning procedure (operational steps)
1) Create release metadata (release id, model tag, rollout strategy) in release control dashboard.
2) Set routing rules with explicit model_tag parameter; use per-tenant override where available.
3) For emergency pin: call admin API PATCH /v1/routing/pin?tenant=<t>&model_tag=<sha> OR flip global feature-flag to previous tag.
4) After pin: run quick verification smoke for that tenant and clear operator notes.

Warmup and cache priming
- Run priming script: 5k low-latency prime requests spread across all regions to populate KV cache. (Priming payloads saved in /ops/priming/pool.json)
- Allow 15–30m for caches to stabilize before opening cohort 2.
- If warmup shows >50% variance in latency between warm/amber nodes, run additional priming for specific shard.

Smoke tests and quick commands (to save in ops snippets)
- smoke.sh --model-tag sha1234 --region us-west1 --count 500 (baseline compare)
- curl -H "X-Model-Tag: sha1234" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @sample.json
- run_promptset_eval.sh --tag sha1234 --suite smoke120 --output /tmp/eval.json

Runbook (steps during ramp)
- Step 0: Confirm green from preflight and warmup. Start Dial 1.
- Step 1: Monitor 15m windows for thresholds above. If stable, move to next dial.
- Step 2: If any automatic trigger fires, escalation: (i) auto-pin, (ii) send DM to on-call, (iii) open incident with prefilled template.
- Step 3: For manual rollback, run admin pin procedure + invalidate client SDK cache (push update if necessary).

Communication plan
- Post rollout commencement: send brief to #releases with release id, cohort sizes, expected impact and contacts.
- If rollback: update thread with root-cause hypothesis and immediate mitigation.
- Postmortem: 48–72h async doc with timeline, metrics, and follow-ups.

Postmortem stub (to copy into new doc)
- Summary
- Timeline (rt timestamps)
- Affected tenants / volume
- What went wrong
- Why existing controls didn't catch it earlier
- Immediate fixes (short)
- Long-term fixes (ownership + ETA)

Open questions / TODOs
- Add a short synthetic that exercises KV cache eviction edge cases (ask infra).
- Validate promptset coverage for LLM hallucination patterns (link to eval deck).
- Decide whether to expose dial levels to self-serve tenants (risk: more noisy experiments).

Notes to self
- Keep dials conservative early in the week (avoid Friday evenings).
- Prefer internal tenant runs during region maintenance windows.
- When in doubt, pause and observe — many regressions show noise before steady trend.

End of scratch — revisit before next scheduled flip.
